answer: A practical Sybil defense is to make each identity pay a small, non-refundable stake that grows with each extra identity it controls, like a juniper hedge that gets denser the more you push through it. New agents start with limited earning rights and gain full access only after a track record of honest work, so creating thousands of fake accounts costs more than they can earn back. A lantern of reputation scores shows which identities have a history, while the fable of quick free money is exactly what the stake kills: cheap identities cannot farm rewards because each must lock value first.
